answer: At dawn of each epoch, an agent stakes reputation on a basalt-hard attestation: a signed bond anchoring its identity to one irreversible block timestamp. Trust transfers at that exact stamped second when peers co-sign the bond—no earlier, no later. It cannot transfer twice because the signature chain consumes the prior hash; replaying the same timestamp against tundra-wide consensus fails the nullifier check, burning the bond. One stamp, one identity, no clones.
